title: Structure of Health Facilities and Social Services
path: Structure of Health Facilities and Social Services

headings.title: Introduction to Healthcare Delivery Systems in Nigeria
headings.content: The Nigerian health system operates on a three-tier structure designed to make healthcare accessible to the entire population. This decentralized framework divides responsibilities among the federal, state, and local governments. The primary goal is to provide a continuum of care where patients enter at the grassroots level and move up only when their medical needs exceed the capacity of lower-tier facilities.

headings.title: Primary Health Facilities
headings.content:
Primary health care represents the first point of contact individuals have with the national health system. These facilities focus heavily on preventive services, health education, and basic curative care for common ailments. 

- **Health Posts**: The smallest unit, usually serving small rural villages with basic community-based outreach.
- **Primary Health Clinics**: Staffed mainly by community health workers and mid-level nurses, providing daily outpatient care and immunizations.
- **Comprehensive Health Centres**: Larger facilities offering maternity services, minor surgical procedures, and round-the-clock observation beds.

headings.title: Secondary Health Facilities
headings.content: Secondary health facilities receive patients referred from the primary level. These are general hospitals and comprehensive cottage hospitals located at the Local Government Area or state level. They provide specialized services in areas such as internal medicine, general surgery, pediatrics, and obstetrics and gynecology. Nurses in these facilities manage inpatient wards, monitor post-surgical recovery, and assist with diagnostic investigations like basic laboratory tests and X-rays.

headings.title: Tertiary Health Facilities
headings.content: Tertiary health facilities sit at the apex of the healthcare delivery pyramid. These include teaching hospitals, federal medical centers, and specialized institutes like orthopedic or psychiatric hospitals. They are equipped with advanced technology and highly specialized personnel capable of managing complex, rare, or critical health conditions. Beyond patient care, tertiary institutions serve as primary training grounds for medical, nursing, and allied health students, as well as hubs for health research.

headings.title: Social Services and Community Support
headings.content: Health is influenced by social, economic, and environmental factors, making social services an integral part of holistic care. Medical social workers collaborate with nursing staff to address non-medical barriers to healing, such as financial distress, domestic abuse, abandonment, and bereavement. In Nigerian hospitals, social welfare departments help indigent patients access charity funds, connect families with community support groups, and coordinate rehabilitation services for individuals living with disabilities.

headings.title: Inter-Referral Pathways and Continuity of Care
headings.content: An effective referral system ensures that patients receive the right level of care at the right time without administrative delays. Referrals typically move upward from primary to secondary and tertiary centers when complications arise, and downward back to primary centers for follow-up once a patient stabilizes. Nurses play a crucial role in this process by writing detailed referral notes, stabilizing the patient for transport, and communicating clinical handover details to receiving facilities.

headings.title: The Role of Nurses Across Different Facility Levels
headings.content: Nursing responsibilities shift dynamically depending on the tier of the health facility. At the primary level, nurses act as public health advocates, managing immunization drives, antenatal clinics, and community health education. In secondary settings, they take on more acute clinical roles, managing surgical wards, administering intravenous therapies, and monitoring vital signs. Tertiary-level nurses specialize further, working in intensive care units, cardiothoracic centers, or renal dialysis units, requiring advanced technical skills and critical reasoning.
